(i) the hitting set problem on collections of cluters can be solved in polynomial time, and (ii) the hitting set problems on collections of MFMC cluters can be approximated within a factor of 1 + epsilon, in polynomial time, for any epsilon > 0.
In summary, our research is concerned with
designing simple and efficient algorithms to solve problems that are related to the maximum concurrent flow problem and the maximum concurrent multicommodity flow problem.
developing efficient algorithms for hitting set problems on a collection of (possibly non-MFMC) clutters.
designing fast approximation algorithms for a class of problems that have been studied extensively in the past.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have given a unified approach for solving these problems and our approach is simple and efficient.
our algorithms are simple, efficient and solve a large number of problems that have not been studied in the past.
our paper is the first one to show that the hitting set problem on any collection of clutters can be solved in polynomial time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a unified framework for solving a variety of problems on collections of (general) clutters.
for any given collection of clutters, if the hitting set problem is NP-hard, we provide a simple algorithm that runs in polynomial time and gives a (1+epsilon)-approximation to the optimum solution.
we give the first FPTAS for the fractional Steiner forest problem, and the first polynomial time algorithms for three other problems on clutters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Steiner forest formulation can be used to obtain efficient algorithms for hitting set problems on collections of arbitrary clutters.
the MFMC property of the clutters is a key factor that can be used to obtain efficient algorithms for these problems.
for a large class of hitting set problems, the existence of an FPTAS is a direct consequence of the existence of an efficient separation oracle for the underlying polytope.
